subject.title: boot-md hook re-runs BOOT.md on every gateway restart

question: Should boot-md remain a per-gateway-startup hook when BOOT.md exists, or should OpenClaw add persisted run-once lifecycle state with an explicit reset path?
rationale: Current docs and runtime define per-startup execution, while the report and production datapoint ask for cross-restart idempotency; implementation needs maintainer intent on state ownership, reset behavior, and compatibility.

options.title: Add persisted run-once lifecycle
options.body: Store BOOT.md completion in an owned state store and provide a documented reset or doctor path for users who want BOOT.md to run again.

options.title: Keep per-startup behavior
options.body: Keep BOOT.md as an every-startup checklist and document disabling or narrowing expensive boot work as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Split remaining symptoms
options.body: Keep this issue focused on lifecycle semantics and track boot-session route ownership or channel-stall bugs in narrower related issues.

recommendation.title: Add persisted run-once lifecycle
recommendation.body: Store BOOT.md completion in an owned state store and provide a documented reset or doctor path for users who want BOOT.md to run again.

likelyOwner.reason: ngutman introduced the boot-md startup hook and is the strongest historical owner for deciding whether its original lifecycle should change.
